question: In 1877, Viceroy Lytton organised a Durbar to acknowledge ______ as the Empress of India.
solution:
The correct option is __**Queen Victoria.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Viceroy Lytton **organised the **Durbar in Delhi** to acknowledge **Queen Victoria** as the **Empress of India.**
 
• **Queen Angelia** is not a **historical figure** and is not related to this event.
 
• **Queen Elizabeth** was** not** the Empress of India, and her reign began much later than **1877.**
 
• **Queen Elizabeth II** was also **not** the Empress of India, and her reign began in the **20th century.**
 
• **Queen Victoria** was the **Queen of England** and **Ireland from 1837** until her death in **1901**.
 
 
• She was also the **Empress of India **from **1877 until 1901**, after the British government decided to bestow this title upon her.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** Durbar **was a grand ceremony that was held to mark the** proclamation of Queen Victoria **as the **Empress of India.**
 
• It was attended by** Indian princes and British officials**, and it was a symbol of **British imperial power.**
 
• The Durbar was held in three different cities:** Allahabad, Delhi, and Lahore.**
 
• The** Delhi Durbar **was the **most famous one**, and it was attended by around **68,000 people.**
 
• Queen Victoria never visited India during her reign as Empress, but she was very interested in **Indian culture and history**.
 
 
• She owned several **Indian artefacts, **and she was known to have a** fondness for Indian cuisine.**
 
 
 
• Queen Elizabeth II visited India several times during her reign, but she **did not hold** the title of Empress of India.
 
 
• The title was** dropped **after India gained independence in** 1947.**
